catalog: CaseAttend Step 1 and foundational-sciences public-domain lesson candidates
scope_note: All vignette seeds and learning objectives below are newly written. NCI entries use text-only source material under NCI's reuse policy; embedded third-party graphics are excluded unless separately cleared. CDC PHIL entries use individual item pages that explicitly state there are no copyright restrictions.

license_authorities.name: National Cancer Institute copyright and reuse policy
license_authorities.evidence: Unless otherwise indicated, NCI product text is free of copyright; NCI requests credit and a link. Only NCI-credited graphics are copyright-free, so this catalog does not clear embedded graphics by implication.

license_authorities.name: CDC Public Health Image Library FAQ
license_authorities.evidence: PHIL explains that public-domain images may be used without permission and requests credit to the originating institution and contributor when known. Each selected item page independently states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'.

candidates.lesson_title: A Murmur at the Mitral Valve: Four-Chamber Flow
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Cardiovascular anatomy; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A 32-year-old with exertional dyspnea has a holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla. Learners trace normal blood flow and predict the pressure and chamber changes caused by mitral regurgitation.
learning_objectives: Trace blood through chambers, valves, and great vessels
Relate valve position to auscultation findings
Predict left atrial and pulmonary venous consequences of regurgitation
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original diagram would show four heart chambers, valves, and directional blood-flow arrows without patient identifiers.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Use page text only; do not import embedded graphics unless explicitly credited to NCI. Cardiology review should verify pressure-volume claims and murmur wording.

candidates.lesson_title: Dropped Beats: Conduction and the Cardiac Cycle
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Cardiovascular physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A 71-year-old with fatigue has intermittent failure of impulses to reach the ventricles. Learners connect the conduction pathway to atrial and ventricular contraction and to changes in cardiac output.
learning_objectives: Sequence sinoatrial, atrioventricular, His-Purkinje activation
Relate electrical activation to systole and diastole
Explain how bradycardia alters cardiac output
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original visual would map the cardiac conduction pathway over a simplified heart outline.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Use text only. Add a newly drawn ECG if desired; electrophysiology review is required before publishing timing claims.

candidates.lesson_title: The Collapsed Lung: Mechanics of Ventilation
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Respiratory physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: After blunt chest trauma, a young adult develops unilateral absent breath sounds and hypotension. Learners use pressure gradients, pleural coupling, and chest-wall recoil to explain the physiology.
learning_objectives: Compare atmospheric, intrapleural, and alveolar pressures
Explain diaphragm-driven inspiration
Predict the effect of pleural air on ventilation and venous return
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed cross-section would compare an expanded lung with a lung separated from the chest wall by pleural air.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Keep the emergency scenario educational, not treatment advice. Pulmonary review should confirm sign conventions and tension-pneumothorax hemodynamics.

candidates.lesson_title: Restrictive or Obstructive? Reading Lung Volumes
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Respiratory physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with progressive dyspnea has reduced vital capacity, while another with smoking history has air trapping. Learners distinguish measurable volumes from calculated capacities and interpret the patterns.
learning_objectives: Define tidal, inspiratory reserve, expiratory reserve, and residual volumes
Calculate major lung capacities
Contrast obstructive air trapping with restrictive volume loss
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original stacked-volume chart would label tidal and reserve volumes and the capacities formed from them.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Source is a conceptual primer, not a complete PFT guide. Add current reference equations and demographic caveats only after specialist review.

candidates.lesson_title: From Glomerulus to Ureter: Localizing an Obstruction
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Renal anatomy and physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with colicky flank pain has hydronephrosis above a ureteral stone. Learners trace filtrate from nephron to collecting system and predict how obstruction changes upstream pressure.
learning_objectives: Identify renal cortex, medulla, calyces, and pelvis
Trace filtrate through nephron and collecting structures
Explain how obstruction can reduce glomerular filtration
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original cutaway would label cortex, medulla, calyces, renal pelvis, and ureter with urine-flow arrows.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Do not reuse embedded illustrations without asset-level clearance. Nephrology review should separate anatomy facts from modeled pressure effects.

candidates.lesson_title: Epigastric Pain: Reading the Stomach Wall
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Gastrointestinal anatomy and histology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with burning epigastric pain has an ulcer extending beyond the mucosa. Learners localize gastric regions and wall layers and connect depth of injury to bleeding and perforation risk.
learning_objectives: Identify cardia, fundus, body, pylorus, and curvatures
Sequence the layers of the gastrointestinal wall
Relate ulcer depth to nearby vessels and peritoneal exposure
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original stomach outline would label its regions and show a magnified wall-layer inset.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Use only cleared text concepts. GI/pathology review should verify ulcer complications and avoid implying endoscopic management guidance.

candidates.lesson_title: Malabsorption versus Colitis: Small and Large Intestine
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Gastrointestinal anatomy and physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: Two patients have chronic diarrhea: one with weight loss and nutrient deficiencies, the other with blood and urgency. Learners compare the structural and functional roles of small and large bowel.
learning_objectives: Trace the regions of small and large intestine
Compare nutrient absorption with water and electrolyte recovery
Use symptom patterns to localize disease broadly
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original tract map would distinguish small-bowel segments from colon segments with neutral colors and labels.
candidates.caution_review_notes: This is localization practice, not diagnosis. Review for oversimplification because several disorders involve both bowel regions.

candidates.lesson_title: Hypertension with Hypokalemia: The Adrenal Cortex
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Endocrine anatomy and physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with resistant hypertension, weakness, and low potassium has suppressed renin. Learners map adrenal cortical zones to hormone classes and distinguish cortical from medullary output.
learning_objectives: Differentiate adrenal cortex from medulla
Map cortical zones to mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, and androgens
Explain how excess aldosterone changes potassium and acid-base balance
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original adrenal cross-section would label three cortical zones and the medulla.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Endocrinology review should verify feedback relationships and avoid conflating primary and secondary hyperaldosteronism.

candidates.lesson_title: Perioral Tingling after Neck Surgery: Thyroid and Parathyroid
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Endocrine anatomy and physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: After thyroid surgery, a patient develops tingling and carpopedal spasm. Learners use gland anatomy and calcium feedback to explain accidental parathyroid injury.
learning_objectives: Describe thyroid and parathyroid relationships
Contrast thyroid hormone and parathyroid hormone functions
Predict calcium and phosphate changes after loss of PTH
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original posterior thyroid view would show the usual parathyroid locations without implying that every patient has identical anatomy.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Explicitly teach anatomic variation. Endocrine/surgical review should check electrolyte predictions and postoperative framing.

candidates.lesson_title: A Child's Growth-Plate Injury
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Musculoskeletal anatomy and physiology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A 12-year-old injures the distal femoral physis during sports. Learners connect endochondral ossification and growth-plate organization to future limb-length risk.
learning_objectives: Contrast intramembranous with endochondral ossification
Explain longitudinal growth at the epiphyseal plate
Predict why physeal injury can cause angular or length disturbance
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original long-bone schematic would mark epiphysis, physis, metaphysis, and diaphysis.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Do not infer fracture classification from this overview. Pediatric orthopedic review should add age and prognosis nuance.

candidates.lesson_title: Weakness after Rhabdomyolysis: Muscle from Fiber to Fascicle
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Muscle anatomy and histology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: After prolonged exertion, a patient has severe muscle pain, weakness, and dark urine. Learners organize skeletal muscle from myofilament to whole muscle and identify where membrane injury releases intracellular contents.
learning_objectives: Organize myofilaments, myofibrils, fibers, fascicles, and muscle
Relate connective-tissue sheaths to muscle structure
Explain why myocyte injury releases creatine kinase and myoglobin
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed nested schematic would show whole muscle, fascicle, fiber, myofibril, and paired thick and thin filaments.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Keep treatment outside scope. Verify terminology and renal-complication links with muscle and renal reviewers.

candidates.lesson_title: A Cell in Hypotonic Fluid: Membrane Transport
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Cell physiology and biochemistry; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A laboratory technician accidentally suspends erythrocytes in markedly hypotonic fluid. Learners predict water movement, cell swelling, and lysis while distinguishing passive from energy-dependent transport.
learning_objectives: Differentiate diffusion, facilitated diffusion, osmosis, and active transport
Predict water movement from relative effective osmolarity
Explain why erythrocytes swell in a hypotonic solution
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed three-panel visual would show erythrocytes in hypertonic, isotonic, and hypotonic solutions.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Use current definitions of osmolarity and tonicity; faculty review should address nonpenetrating versus penetrating solutes.

candidates.lesson_title: Checkpoint Failure: Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Pathology and molecular biology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A tumor panel shows an activating growth-signaling variant and biallelic loss of a checkpoint gene. Learners distinguish gain-of-function proto-oncogene activation from loss-of-function tumor-suppressor failure.
learning_objectives: Contrast proto-oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
Relate gain- and loss-of-function changes to cellular behavior
Explain why multiple cooperating alterations promote malignancy
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original comparison would depict a stuck accelerator for excessive growth signaling and failed brakes for checkpoint loss.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Do not repeat outdated gene-count statements on the source page. Molecular pathology review must update all examples and nomenclature.

candidates.lesson_title: Why Antimetabolites Target S Phase
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Cell cycle and pharmacology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A rapidly dividing malignancy is treated with a DNA-synthesis inhibitor. Learners place the drug's greatest effect within the cell cycle and anticipate effects on other proliferative tissues.
learning_objectives: Sequence G1, S, G2, and M phases
Identify DNA synthesis as an S-phase event
Connect proliferative fraction to therapeutic effect and toxicity
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed circular cell-cycle diagram would mark G1, S, G2, M, and an optional G0 branch.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Avoid implying perfect phase specificity. Oncology/pharmacology review should handle scheduling and toxicity nuance.

candidates.lesson_title: A Midline Mass: Germ-Layer Derivatives
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Embryology and pathology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: An adolescent has a heterogeneous sacrococcygeal mass containing cartilage, epithelium, and neural tissue. Learners use the three germ layers to explain the mixed histology.
learning_objectives: Name ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm
Associate representative adult tissues with each germ layer
Explain why a teratoma may contain tissues from multiple layers
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original three-column chart would map germ layers to selected derivative tissues.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Embryology review is essential because germ-layer derivative lists often become overgeneralized. Avoid using pathology images without separate clearance.

candidates.lesson_title: Carcinoma or Sarcoma? Tissue of Origin
candidates.domain_artifact_type: General pathology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: Two masses arise in the same limb: one from gland-forming epithelium and another from connective tissue. Learners classify each by tissue of origin rather than location alone.
learning_objectives: Distinguish epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous tissues
Classify carcinomas and sarcomas by origin
Separate histogenesis from anatomic site
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed comparison would show simplified epithelial sheets and connective-tissue matrix without reproducing histology slides.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Pathology review should account for mixed, hematolymphoid, melanocytic, and poorly differentiated neoplasms.

candidates.lesson_title: Benign, In Situ, or Invasive? Classifying a Neoplasm
candidates.domain_artifact_type: General pathology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A biopsy shows atypical epithelial cells that either remain above or cross a basement membrane in two alternate versions of the case. Learners use behavior and invasion to choose the correct category.
learning_objectives: Differentiate benign and malignant behavior
Define in situ disease and invasion
Relate basement-membrane breach to metastatic potential
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed two-panel schematic would compare atypical cells confined above a basement membrane with cells invading below it.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Use precise organ-specific terminology; not every tumor system uses the same in-situ framework.

candidates.lesson_title: From Symptom to Tissue Diagnosis
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Diagnostic pathology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with weight loss has an abnormal scan and then a biopsy. Learners order the steps from clinical suspicion through tissue acquisition, microscopic diagnosis, and staging workup.
learning_objectives: Distinguish screening, diagnosis, grading, and staging
Explain why histopathology can establish tumor identity
Identify questions that require imaging versus tissue
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed original flow diagram would move from symptom and exam to imaging, biopsy, pathology report, and staging.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Avoid presenting a universal workflow; diagnostic sequences vary by tumor and patient context.

candidates.lesson_title: Reading a Surgical Pathology Report
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Diagnostic pathology; NCI/SEER text reference
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A resection report lists specimen, histologic type, grade, margins, lymphovascular invasion, and nodes. Learners translate each element into a concise problem representation.
learning_objectives: Identify core components of a pathology report
Differentiate histologic type from grade
Explain how margins and nodes affect subsequent interpretation
candidates.license_label: NCI product text free of copyright under NCI reuse policy, unless otherwise indicated
candidates.attribution: Credit National Cancer Institute and link the original NCI/SEER page.
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Text source; proposed synthetic report would use fictional data and visually separate diagnosis, grade, margins, and nodes.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Create a wholly synthetic report; never use patient data. Pathologist review should ensure realistic phrasing and organ-specific caveats.

candidates.lesson_title: Rust-Colored Sputum: Pneumococcus on Gram Stain
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Bacteriology; CDC PHIL light micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: An older adult with fever, pleuritic pain, and lobar consolidation has gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci in sputum. Learners connect morphology, capsule, and splenic clearance.
learning_objectives: Recognize the classic Gram-stain arrangement of Streptococcus pneumoniae
Explain the capsule's role in virulence
Relate asplenia to risk from encapsulated bacteria
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; contributor Arnold Kaufman (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Gram-stained field containing many purple paired, tapered bacterial cells among larger host-cell material.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Historic teaching image; verify stain labeling and current diagnostic workflow. Do not infer antimicrobial susceptibility from morphology.

candidates.lesson_title: Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: C. difficile Morphology
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Bacteriology; CDC PHIL scanning electron micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: After broad-spectrum antibiotics, a hospitalized patient develops watery diarrhea and leukocytosis. Learners separate organism morphology from toxin-mediated pathogenesis and testing.
learning_objectives: Describe Clostridioides difficile as a spore-forming anaerobic bacillus
Explain how antibiotic disruption permits overgrowth
Connect toxins to colonic epithelial injury
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; Lois S. Wiggs; photograph Janice Carr (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Scanning electron micrograph showing numerous elongated bacterial cells on an irregular background surface.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Electron-microscope contrast is not a Gram-stain result. Use current taxonomy and testing guidance; image alone cannot diagnose infection.

candidates.lesson_title: Intracellular Diplococci: Gonococcal Urethritis
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Bacteriology; CDC PHIL Gram-stain micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A young adult has dysuria and purulent urethral discharge. A smear shows gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils, prompting a lesson on morphology, antigenic variation, and confirmatory testing.
learning_objectives: Recognize intracellular gram-negative diplococci
Explain how antigenic variation impairs durable immunity
Distinguish suggestive microscopy from definitive nucleic-acid testing
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; contributor Joe Miller (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Gram-stained field with pink paired cocci located within and around larger purple-stained inflammatory cells.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Use non-stigmatizing language and current CDC diagnostic/treatment references. Microscopy performance varies by specimen and population.

candidates.lesson_title: Acid-Fast Bacilli in a Chronic Cough
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Bacteriology; CDC PHIL fluorochrome-stain micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with weeks of cough, night sweats, and weight loss has fluorescent slender organisms on a concentrated respiratory specimen. Learners explain acid-fast staining and the need for culture or molecular confirmation.
learning_objectives: Relate mycolic-acid-rich walls to acid-fast staining
Interpret a positive smear as evidence of acid-fast organisms, not species proof
Distinguish smear, culture, and nucleic-acid roles
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; contributor Wilbur D. Jones (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Dark microscopy field containing scattered bright yellow-green slender rods and small fluorescent clusters.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Fluorescence does not establish M. tuberculosis species. Infection-control and diagnostic claims require current public-health review.

candidates.lesson_title: Two Plates, Two Outcomes: Tuberculosis Drug Susceptibility
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Bacteriology and pharmacology; CDC PHIL culture-plate photograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A culture isolate grows on a control medium and on one drug-containing medium but not another. Learners infer phenotypic resistance while separating laboratory susceptibility from bedside regimen selection.
learning_objectives: Explain the logic of growth-control and drug-containing media
Interpret growth in the presence of a drug as phenotypic resistance
Differentiate susceptibility testing from direct microscopic identification
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Laboratory culture media arranged for comparison, with visible growth differing between control and antimicrobial-containing conditions.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Historic method illustration. Do not teach current breakpoints or regimens from the image; microbiology review must update methods.

candidates.lesson_title: What the Coronavirus Illustration Can and Cannot Show
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Virology; CDC PHIL scientific illustration
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A learner mistakes a widely used SARS-CoV-2 illustration for an electron micrograph. The case asks them to identify envelope and surface proteins while distinguishing conceptual art from measured structure.
learning_objectives: Identify the viral envelope and spike proteins represented
Relate spike-mediated attachment to entry
Distinguish a scientific illustration from a microscopy image
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; Alissa Eckert, MSMI, and Dan Higgins, MAMS (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Three-dimensional illustration of a spherical enveloped virus with many red club-shaped surface projections and smaller orange and yellow surface proteins.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Label explicitly as an illustration, not a literal scale model or micrograph. Update variant-specific claims separately.

candidates.lesson_title: Budding from a Lymphocyte: The HIV Life Cycle
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Virology; CDC PHIL scanning electron micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with recurrent opportunistic infections has a low CD4 count. Learners use a micrograph of viral budding to place entry, reverse transcription, integration, assembly, and maturation in sequence.
learning_objectives: Sequence major steps of the HIV replication cycle
Relate budding to acquisition of a viral envelope
Map major antiretroviral classes to replication steps
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; C. Goldsmith, P. Feorino, E. L. Palmer, W. R. McManus; photograph C. Goldsmith (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Scanning electron micrograph showing multiple round viral particles at and near the surface of a larger lymphocyte.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Use person-first language. Micrograph cannot determine viral load or treatment response; pharmacology must be updated to current standards.

candidates.lesson_title: Bullet-Shaped Virions and Negri Bodies
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Virology and neuropathology; CDC PHIL transmission electron micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: After an unrecognized animal exposure, a patient develops hydrophobia and encephalitic symptoms. Learners connect rabies morphology, retrograde axonal transport, and cytoplasmic inclusions.
learning_objectives: Recognize the characteristic bullet-shaped rhabdovirus morphology
Explain retrograde neuronal spread to the central nervous system
Identify Negri bodies as a classic pathologic clue
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; contributor and photographer Dr. Fred Murphy (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Transmission electron micrograph showing multiple bullet-shaped viral particles and adjacent dense cellular inclusion material.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Historic image. Exposure management is time-critical and must use current public-health guidance; do not imply Negri bodies are required for diagnosis.

candidates.lesson_title: Ring Forms in Erythrocytes: Falciparum Malaria
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Parasitology; CDC PHIL blood-smear micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A traveler returns with episodic fever, anemia, and thrombocytopenia. A thin smear shows delicate ring forms, including more than one parasite in some erythrocytes.
learning_objectives: Recognize ring-stage malaria parasites in erythrocytes
List smear features that can support P. falciparum identification
Relate parasitized erythrocytes to hemolysis and microvascular disease
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; contributor Dr. Mae Melvin (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Stained thin blood film containing red blood cells, several with small blue-purple ring-shaped intracellular forms.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Do not diagnose species from a single cropped field without expert review. Add current travel, testing, and severity criteria separately.

candidates.lesson_title: Two Forms, One Protozoan: Giardia's Life Cycle
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Parasitology; CDC PHIL life-cycle illustration
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A camper develops foul-smelling diarrhea, bloating, and weight loss after drinking untreated stream water. Learners follow cyst ingestion, excystation, trophozoite colonization, and cyst shedding.
learning_objectives: Distinguish Giardia cyst and trophozoite forms
Identify the environmentally resistant infective stage
Connect small-intestinal colonization to malabsorptive symptoms
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; Alexander J. da Silva, PhD, and Melanie Moser (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Circular life-cycle diagram showing ingestion of cysts, intestinal trophozoites, encystation, and cysts leaving the host.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Redraw labels only if preserving scientific meaning. Keep prevention and treatment aligned with current CDC guidance.

candidates.lesson_title: Seizures from a Larval Cestode: Neurocysticercosis
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Parasitology and neuropathology; CDC PHIL specimen photograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient with new-onset seizures has multiple calcified and cystic brain lesions. Learners distinguish ingestion of T. solium eggs causing cysticercosis from ingestion of larval cysts causing intestinal taeniasis.
learning_objectives: Differentiate taeniasis from cysticercosis routes
Identify humans as potential intermediate hosts after egg ingestion
Relate lesion location and inflammation to neurologic symptoms
candidates.license_label: U.S. public domain; item page states 'Copyright Restrictions: None'
candidates.attribution: Courtesy CDC; contributor Dr. George R. Healy (credit requested by PHIL).
candidates.accessibility_neutral_image_description: Clinical specimen photograph showing several pale, rounded larval cyst structures against a plain background.
candidates.caution_review_notes: Potentially graphic specimen; provide a content note and non-image equivalent. Avoid stigmatizing geographic or dietary assumptions.

candidates.lesson_title: Germ Tubes in Serum: Identifying Candida albicans
candidates.domain_artifact_type: Mycology; CDC PHIL light micrograph
candidates.case_vignette_seed: A patient receiving broad-spectrum antibiotics develops oral plaques. A yeast isolate forms tube-like outgrowths after incubation in serum.
learning_objectives: Describe budding yeast and germ-tube morphology
Explain the principle and limitations of the germ-tube test
Relate antibiotic pressure and immune status to candidiasis risk
